Marine & underwater services · Interim CEO & board · Board & Interim Leadership, Value Creation

Taking the CEO seat in a lender-backed turnaround

When a sponsor- and lender-controlled marine services operator hit a liquidity wall, we did not advise from the sidelines. A member of our founding team took the CEO seat and ran the recovery.

The situation
The business had entered a decisive stabilisation phase: a liquidity strain, eroding revenue and margin, uneven reporting and fragmented accountability, all under a lender forbearance framework.
What we did
Stepped into the CEO role and installed a coordinated recovery: narrowed more than twenty scattered initiatives to a Top-5 enterprise priority set (liquidity, dynamic pricing, operational reliability and utilisation, revenue acceleration, and governance discipline); stood up a disciplined lender-reporting rhythm (13-week cash flow, weekly liquidity review, clear escalation protocols); enforced spend controls through an approval and authority matrix; and reset the leadership cadence with weekly executive huddles and a hands-on execution workshop.
The outcome
Rebuilt lender and board credibility, restored margin and cash discipline, and set the business on a path to interest-service readiness.
We don't just advise the turnaround. We take the seat and run it, from the lender report to the shop floor.
Team engagement, prior to Navex.
Marine services · Private equity sponsors · Strategic Advisory for PE (deal sourcing)

A proprietary way into a fragmented segment

Generalist funds struggle to enter marine services: it is fragmented, relationship-driven and under-covered. We gave sponsors an operator's way in.

The situation
PE sponsors wanted differentiated entry points into the fragmented marine-services segment, a niche that rewards specific industry knowledge, operator relationships and access to talent in lower-cost jurisdictions, and is therefore overlooked by generalist funds.
What we did
Authored an operator-grade maritime investment thesis and built a proprietary target screen across sub-segments: third-party ship management, inspection, survey and testing, engineering and project management, maritime technology, safety and training, and environmental or regulation-driven services. Profiled candidates on a consistent template (positioning, service mix, recurring-revenue quality, switching costs, and a buy-and-build or carve-out angle) and framed an integrated marine-services platform consolidation play.
The outcome
A structured, thesis-led pipeline that let sponsors move quickly on well-positioned, recurring-revenue assets, with a clear consolidation roadmap.
Sourcing grounded in operating knowledge, not a broker's pitch.
Team engagement, prior to Navex.
Multi-region operator · Value Creation & Growth Planning

Standing up a value-creation office after close

A newly acquired operator could not see its own margins clearly. We built the machine that let management run the value-creation thesis.

The situation
Decentralised processes, inconsistent KPIs and low data quality were obscuring margin, utilisation and pipeline, and slowing the value-creation thesis.
What we did
Established a Transformation Office as the single quarterback across internal teams and external partners: defined the target operating model, standardised SOPs and accountabilities, set enterprise KPI definitions, and built a three-tier analytics layer (commercial, financial and project profitability) on a single source of truth, sequenced by enterprise impact with clear governance and escalation.
The outcome
One consistent view of performance, faster and cleaner decisions, and a value-creation plan management could actually execute and track.
Enterprise value over local optimisation. Clarity before automation.
Team engagement, prior to Navex.
